item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The District Administration Office (DAO), Siraha, has lifted the curfew imposed in Golbazar Municipality following an improvement in the security situation.

In a notice issued on Sunday, the DAO Siraha said the decision was taken after reviewing the latest security situation in the municipality. “The curfew order has been lifted with effect from 7 pm on Sunday in accordance with Section 6(9A) of the Local Administration Act, 1971,” the notice, issued by Chief District Officer Surendra Paudel, said.

The curfew had been imposed from 2 pm on Thursday after locals took to the street to protest police firing in Sunsari on Sunday night. Ganesh Yadav (17) of Tulsipur in Aurahi Rural Municipality-2 died when the curfew was in place.

During the unrest, protesters set fire to AB Mall, more than a dozen private houses and shops in Golbazar, as well as 20 motorcycles and an autorickshaw.

Yadav’s family accepted his body after Minister for Home Affairs Sudhan Gurung reached the incident site and assured the family of a fair investigation. The minister also announced a compensation of Rs 1 million for the bereaved family and expressed commitment to provide employment for one member of the family.

item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The District Administration Office, Saptari, has lifted the curfew imposed in Rajbiraj Municipality and Bodebarsain Municipality.

However, it has issued a prohibitory order barring gatherings of more than five people, as well as public meetings, rallies, sit-ins and demonstrations in both municipalities until further notice as per Section 6 3(A) of the Local Administration Act, 1971.

According to a notice issued by Chief District Officer Shyam Krishna Thapa, the decision to enforce the prohibitory order was taken at a meeting of the District Security Committee held on Sunday.

The restricted area in Rajbiraj Municipality extends from the Khando River in the east to the Jamuni Thalahi section of the Hulaki Highway in the west, from Basbitti Chowk on Rupani Road in the north to the Koshi Western Main Canal in the south.

Similarly, in Bodebarsain Municipality, the prohibitory order covers the area from Khadka Bridge on the Hulaki Highway in the east to Pritampur Chowk in the west, and from Negada Chowk in the north to Manraja Chowk in the south.

Unrest in several Tarai districts of Koshi and Madhesh Provinces, which started following the death of one youth in police firing in Sunsari on July 19, is gradually subsiding.

item.title: Key takeaways from PM Shah’s two-hour meeting with Madhesh leaders
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: Leaders of Madhesh-based political parties have described their meeting with Prime Minister Balendra Shah as positive. After the meeting at the Office of the Prime Minister on Friday, they said the prime minister was receptive to their concerns and expressed commitment to addressing the recent unrest in the Tarai-Madhesh region. Prime Minister Shah invited […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Leaders of Madhesh-based political parties have described their meeting with Prime Minister Balendra Shah as positive.

After the meeting at the Office of the Prime Minister on Friday, they said the prime minister was receptive to their concerns and expressed commitment to addressing the recent unrest in the Tarai-Madhesh region.

Prime Minister Shah invited leaders of Madhesh-based political parties for a discussion after unrest, triggered by police firing in Sunsari on Sunday night, expanded to most of the Tarai districts in Koshi and Madhesh provinces.

“We had heard that the prime minister is not interactive and does not prefer dialogue. There were also doubts about whether he could speak Maithili,” Ram Kumar Sharma, a former Constituent Assembly member, told Himal Press over the phone. “The discussion lasted for two hours and was highly interactive. The prime minister communicated in both Nepali and Maithili. The meeting was very positive.”

Sharma said the leaders offered suggestions to resolve the recent problems in the Tarai-Madhesh region and that the prime minister appeared sensitive to the issues and committed to finding solutions.

He said the leaders told the prime minister that a minor clash had escalated into communal violence, partly due to remarks made by the police.

“We told the prime minister that statements by the Inspector General of Police, such as claims that the number of Rohingya entering Nepal through India was increasing and that the person killed in Sunsari had not died from police firing but from someone else’s bullet, contributed to inflaming communal tensions,” Sharma said. “Although violence erupted, the situation worsened because the home minister did not respond proactively.”

According to Sharma, the leaders also informed the prime minister that the government’s shortcomings had contributed to the escalation of violence and that the unrest appeared to be planned rather than spontaneous.

“This was the first time the prime minister held discussions with Madhesh-based political parties. We believe the meeting was very positive,” Raut said. “We also offered suggestions on resolving the problems seen in several Tarai districts.”

The Madhesh-based parties urged Prime Minister Shah to take the personal initiative to resolve the recent tensions in the Tarai-Madhesh region.

Janamat Party Chair Dr. CK Raut also described the meeting as constructive.

“This was the first time the prime minister held discussions with Madhesh-based political parties. We believe the meeting was very positive,” Raut said. “We also offered suggestions on resolving the problems seen in several Tarai districts.”

Raut said the recent unrest was not a new phenomenon and called for long-term measures to address the underlying issues.

“We suggested forming a rapid action team to deal with such incidents. We also proposed regular security briefings, capacity-building for security personnel and stronger community-level monitoring,” he said.

Rastriya Mukti Party Chairperson Rajendra Mahato said the leaders urged the government to implement agreements reached with the Madhesh movement by previous governments. He also called on the government to intensify its efforts to resolve the ongoing tensions in Madhesh, investigate the Sunsari incident and address the issues in time.

Samim Miyan Ansari, founding chair of the Muslim Commission, said they held in-depth discussions with the prime minister on the issue, suggested measures to restore normalcy and bring those responsible for the incident to justice,” Ansari said.

During the meeting, the leaders also questioned Prime Minister Shah about his views on federalism. In response, Shah urged them not to regard him as anti-federalism.

“I am not against federalism. Please do not doubt my commitment to it,” Sharma quoted the prime minister as saying. “Our party has never decided to oppose federalism. We are committed to strengthening it and to making the provincial structure more effective.”

The Madhesh-based leaders also urged the prime minister to immediately transfer policing and administrative authority to the provinces in accordance with the Constitution.

“We suggested that the provincial governments should be given control over the police immediately, as envisaged in the constitution,” Sharma said. “This would enable provincial governments to respond quickly and effectively to incidents like those seen recently.”

According to the leaders, Prime Minister Shah assured them that he would personally take the initiative to resolve the recent problems in the Tarai-Madhesh region.

item.title: Madhesh-centric parties call for restraint, social harmony
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: Four Madhesh-centric political parties have issued a joint appeal calling for restraint and communal harmony, while demanding an independent judicial investigation into the recent violence in the Tarai. Mahanta Thakur of JSP Nepal, Rajendra Mahato of Rastriya Mukti Party Nepal, Jayakant Raut of Janamat Party, Samim Ansari of Rastriya Nirman Dal, and former Constituent […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Four Madhesh-centric political parties have issued a joint appeal calling for restraint and communal harmony, while demanding an independent judicial investigation into the recent violence in the Tarai.

Mahanta Thakur of JSP Nepal, Rajendra Mahato of Rastriya Mukti Party Nepal, Jayakant Raut of Janamat Party, Samim Ansari of Rastriya Nirman Dal, and former Constituent Assembly member Ram Kumar Sharma issued a joint statement on Thursday, urging Prime Minister Balendra Shah to address the nation and reassure the public about the government’s commitment to peace, social harmony, justice and the rule of law.

They also demanded that those killed in the recent incidents be declared martyrs, with compensation provided to their families and employment opportunities arranged to ensure their long-term livelihoods.

The parties called for a thorough investigation into whether the violence had been instigated by external elements and urged the government to uncover the facts behind the incidents.

They further demanded that the Home Minister take moral responsibility for the incidents and that security personnel involved in the use of force be suspended pending the outcome of the investigation.

They also urged the government to provide free medical treatment for all those injured during the unrest.

The leaders also demanded the formation of a high-level judicial inquiry commission led by a retired Supreme Court Justice to investigate all recent incidents.

Appealing to people to exercise restraint and preserve social harmony, they warned that hatred and provocation would only deepen divisions in society.

item.dc:creator: bishnu

The curfew came into effect at 3:30 pm on Thursday and will remain in force until further notice. Chief District Officer Prem Prasad Luitel […]
item.content:encoded:
JANAKPURDHAM: The District Administration Office, Dhanusha, has imposed an indefinite curfew in Janakpurdham Sub-metropolitan City and other areas from Tuesday afternoon, citing heightened security concerns following recent tensions in neighboring Sunsari.

The curfew came into effect at 3:30 pm on Thursday and will remain in force until further notice.

Chief District Officer Prem Prasad Luitel said the curfew was imposed under Section 6 (A) of the Local Administration Act, 1971, following a decision by the District Security Committee.

Under the order, all movement, public gatherings, rallies, demonstrations, meetings and sit-ins are prohibited within the designated areas during the curfew.

The curfew covers areas all areas of Janakpurdham sub-metropolis, the stretch from Laxmaniya Haat Bazaar Chowk in Laxmaniya-7 westward via Sinurjoda Chowk to Laxmipur Bagewa, the area from MQ Steel on Belauni Road to the petrol pump located 500 metres to the east, the section from the Hulaki Highway to the National Primary School, the Nagarain Municipality area up to Nagarain Chowk, and the Sinurjoda–Sohani–Manimandap–Nepal Nursery–ISKCON Janakpur–Dudhmati Bridge–Bela–Kadari Mosque corridor.

The administration said the curfew was necessary to maintain peace, security and public order.

item.title: Graft case filed against former Madhesh finance minister, six others
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: The Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) has filed a corruption case at the Special Court against seven individuals, including a former Madhesh province finance minister and the then mayor of Bagmati Municipality, over alleged corruption in the under-construction Bagmati Fun Park and Resort project in Sarlahi district. According to the […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) has filed a corruption case at the Special Court against seven individuals, including a former Madhesh province finance minister and the then mayor of Bagmati Municipality, over alleged corruption in the under-construction Bagmati Fun Park and Resort project in Sarlahi district.

According to the CIAA, its study concluded that the preparation of the detailed project report (DPR) for the second phase of the project, approval of the cost estimate, bidding process, and setting of complicated criteria in the bid evaluation process to benefit a limited number of construction companies were carried out through collusion.

The anti-graft body has claimed that the alleged irregularities caused a loss of Rs 393.966 million to the state.

The CIAA alleged that structures that had not been deemed necessary in the original DPR for the first phase were included in the second phase, and a new DPR was prepared without sufficient study of the project’s necessity, risk analysis and financial returns. It also said that the criteria for evaluating bids were designed to limit competition and that conditions favorable to a construction company were included.

The CIAA has sought a fine equivalent to Rs 350 million each from then Madhesh Province Finance Minister Shailendra Prasad Sah and then Secretary Gajendra Kumar Thakur.

Similarly, it has sought a fine of Rs 393.9 million each from then Bagmati Municipality Mayor Bharat Kumar Thapa, Deputy Mayor Lila Kumari Muktan and Chief Administrative Officer Bimal Kumar Pokharel. The CIAA has sought a fine of Rs 200 million from then Undersecretary Uddhav Raj Neupane.

Likewise, BKOI-Dhulikhel JV and its authorized representative, Yubraj Pokharel, have been charged with assisting the main accused. The CIAA has sought punishment equivalent to that of the principal accused under the Corruption Prevention Act from Pokharel and the company.

He was airlifted to Kathmandu on Friday and admitted to the Kathmandu Cleft and Burn Center in Kirtipur, where he had been receiving treatment. Dr. Kiran Nakarmi of the Kathmandu Cleft and Burn Center confirmed Mandal’s […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Bibek Mandal, who set himself on fire on Friday, died from his injuries on Sunday while undergoing treatment.

He was airlifted to Kathmandu on Friday and admitted to the Kathmandu Cleft and Burn Center in Kirtipur, where he had been receiving treatment.

Dr. Kiran Nakarmi of the Kathmandu Cleft and Burn Center confirmed Mandal’s death.

Mandal is the third person to die after attempting self-immolation in the past six days. Earlier, Ganesh Nepali of Mugu and Ashwini Raut of Kathmandu also succumbed to burn injuries while undergoing treatment after setting themselves on fire.

The deceased have been identified as Shabnam Khatun (12), her sister Rubina Khatun (10) and their brother Saiful Sheikh (7). Preliminary investigations show the children drowned while swimming in the pit, Siraha Police Spokesperson DSP Ramesh Bahadur […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Three siblings drowned while swimming in a water-filled pit in Golbazar Municipality-7 of Siraha on Sunday afternoon.

The deceased have been identified as Shabnam Khatun (12), her sister Rubina Khatun (10) and their brother Saiful Sheikh (7).

Preliminary investigations show the children drowned while swimming in the pit, Siraha Police Spokesperson DSP Ramesh Bahadur Pal told Himal Press over the phone.

Locals rescued the siblings and rushed them to a hospital for treatment. However, all three were declared dead on arrival.

Police say further investigation into the incident is underway.

item.title: Task force formed to resolve Madhesh budget disputes
item.dc:creator: bishnu

During a meeting of the Madhesh Provincial Assembly on Sunday, Speaker Ram Ashish Yadav announced the formation of the task force. The task force includes lawmakers Upendra Mahato, Hari […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: A task force has been formed to resolve disputes surrounding the Madhesh Province Government’s budget for the upcoming fiscal year 2026/27 and other related issues.

During a meeting of the Madhesh Provincial Assembly on Sunday, Speaker Ram Ashish Yadav announced the formation of the task force.

The task force includes lawmakers Upendra Mahato, Hari Narayan Mahato, Jangilal Rai, Pramod Kumar Yadav, Sanjay Kumar Yadav, Bimala Ansari Tarun and Sarita Kumari Thakur.

The task force will formulate its own terms of reference and operating procedures.

Meanwhile, Minister for Finance Yubaraj Bhattarai has tabled the Appropriation Bill, 2026 for approval in the provincial assembly.

Speaker Yadav also announced that the provincial assembly had, by a majority vote, approved a proposal moved by lawmaker Rabindra Shrestha to suspend Sub-rules (2) and (3) of Rule 135 of the Madhesh Provincial Assembly Rules.

Following the suspension of the two sub-rules, the Speaker removed the remaining items from Sunday’s agenda.

The next meeting of the Provincial Assembly has been scheduled for 1:00 pm on Tuesday, Asar 30 (mid-July).

The provincial assembly proceedings had remained stalled since July 1 due to obstruction by opposition parties—Janata Samajbadi Party (JSP) Nepal, Janamat Party and Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), demanding amendments to the budget.

The meeting had been convened to hold deliberations on the Appropriation Bill tabled by the provincial government on the same day.

Finance Minister Bhattarai had unveiled a budget of Rs 41.13 billion for fiscal year 2026/27.

item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: A 35-year-old man attempted self-immolation in Sarlahi on Friday.

Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) lawmaker from Sarlahi-4, Amresh Kumar Singh, said Bibek Mandal from Godaita Municipality-10 of Sarlahi set himself on fire on Friday afternoon.

The incident comes a day after Ganesh Nepali of Mugu set himself on fire at Tripureshwar, Kathmandu on Thursday. Nepal succumbed to burn injuries at the Bir Hospital on Friday morning.

Lawmaker Singh said he had notified Prime Minister Balendra Shah, Minister for Home Affairs Sudan Gurung and RSP President Rabi Lamichhane about the incident.

In a social media post, Singh said he had requested the Prime Minister, the Home Minister and the party president to ensure free medical treatment for him. “A helicopter was dispatched immediately after I informed the Prime Minister and arrangements have also been made for his treatment at no cost,” Singh wrote on his Facebook page.
